LearningOutcomes: Students will identify common construction materials, describe their key properties, and justify material selection for given building applications.
LectureTopics: Classification of construction materials: natural and manufactured
Properties of concrete, cement, aggregates, and water
Timber types and grading for construction use
Bricks, blocks, and masonry materials used in Zambian construction
AssessmentMethods: Written quiz on material properties and a practical material identification exercise
FeedbackComments: Excellent coverage of local materials. Include samples from Northern Province suppliers where possible.

LearningOutcomes: Students will describe the main systems of a motor vehicle, explain how they interact, and apply basic workshop safety procedures.
LectureTopics: Overview of motor vehicle systems: engine, transmission, brakes, steering, and electrical
Workshop safety rules and personal protective equipment
Introduction to hand tools and workshop equipment
Vehicle identification: VIN, engine codes, and service history
AssessmentMethods: Practical workshop safety demonstration and short written quiz on vehicle systems
FeedbackComments: Good introduction. Emphasise safety demonstration before allowing students on the workshop floor.

Topic: Overview of Agricultural Engineering in Zambia
LearningOutcomes: Students will explain the scope of agricultural engineering, describe its importance to Zambian food security, and identify key challenges facing the sector in Northern Province.
LectureTopics: Definition and scope of agricultural engineering
Role of agricultural engineering in Zambia's agricultural sector
Challenges and opportunities for agricultural engineering in Northern Province
Overview of course structure and career pathways
AssessmentMethods: Class discussion participation and short reflective essay on agricultural engineering in the local community
FeedbackComments: Very relevant local context. Consider inviting a ZNFU representative for a guest talk.

LearningOutcomes: Students will interpret architectural drawings, identify standard drawing conventions and symbols, and relate drawing information to construction activities.
LectureTopics: Types of construction drawings: architectural, structural, and services
Drawing conventions: scales, dimensions, and notation
Standard symbols used in building drawings
Practical: reading and extracting information from a set of house plans
AssessmentMethods: Practical drawing interpretation exercise and written questions on drawing conventions
FeedbackComments: Well-prepared. Ensure students have access to drawing instruments before the session.

LearningOutcomes: Students will apply a structured diagnostic approach to identify engine faults, use basic diagnostic tools, and interpret fault codes from OBD systems.
LectureTopics: Structured fault diagnosis methodology: symptom, check, test, repair
Introduction to OBD-II systems and fault code interpretation
Using a scan tool for reading live engine data
Practical: performing a basic engine health check on a workshop vehicle
AssessmentMethods: Practical engine health check report and short written test on diagnostic procedures
FeedbackComments: Pending review by Head of Department.
